title: Thrive Quick Fit
subtitle: Build spec, version 1
meta: September 4, 2026  |  Prepared for Sam Chacko, LOFT City Church  |  Status: ready for build

sections.h: The one thing this has to do

blocks.text: Get a newcomer at a welcome lunch from "I don't know where I fit" to a scheduled First Serve with a named team leader, in under five minutes, with a human follow-up inside 48 hours. Everything else is optional.

rows: Planning Center workflow card step 1 completed with a date
Measured in the app, reported in the notification
Anil and Morgan keep using it after the pilot

items: Scope: Quick Fit only. The Full Profile (12-page plan, workplace endowments, growth kits) is deferred until Quick Fit proves itself.
Backend: Planning Center integration from day one. Planning Center is the system of record. No Google Sheets, no separate dashboard, no shared-key page.
Pilot teams: Worship (Anil Varughese) and Family Ministries (Morgan Williams). Both leaders own the 48-hour follow-up personally.
Home: a GitHub repository deployed to thrive.loftcity.church, maintained with Claude Code so Sam and Nincy can change content without touching code.

Brand: the rebuild adopts the June 2026 brand system (navy #1A2E52, orange #E15628, cream, light blue, Barlow Condensed and DM Sans). The current prototype uses the older navy and Raleway/Lato and should be retired when this launches.

blocks.text: A QR code on each table tent opens thrive.loftcity.church. Table hosts are briefed to ask "what did you get?" once people finish. The whole flow is built for one hand, one phone, and a plate on the table.

rows: "Where can you serve?" First name, last name, email. One consent line: LOFT may contact you about serving. Start.
38 quick statements, six per screen, rated from "I would struggle here" to "I would thrive here." Progress vine at the top.
Readiness check on the top five wired areas: "Have you done this kind of thing before?" Four taps.
"Who are you most drawn to serve?" Up to three chips (babies, kids, teens, young adults, adults, seniors, guests, people far from God, people in crisis, behind the scenes).
"How available are you this season?" One tap from six options, including rest and healing and life is very full.
Results: your two Fruitful areas in one sentence each, then two or three specific LOFT roles with real time cost and a Try It Once button.
Tap Try It Once. Confirmation: "Morgan will reach out by Wednesday. Here is what a first Sunday looks like." Optional: pick a second role, or Save For Later.

blocks.text: What was removed from the front door on purpose: work, field, work mode, and the long explanatory paragraphs. Those belong in the Full Profile. Availability stays because the matching engine needs it.
One screen, no scrolling required to reach the action. Designed to be read aloud to a table host.

items: Headline: "[First name], you are wired as a Host and a Teacher." One sentence each, in the garden language.

Role cards (two or three): team name, one line on what you actually do, Sunday or weekday, real time cost from the role catalog (for example "Sunday mornings, 8:15 to 12:00, twice a month"), leader first name, Try It Once button.
A collapsed line: "See your full picture" reveals Faithful and Wearying areas and all twelve scores. Present, but not in the way.
For someone in a season of rest: the same screen, but the button reads Save For Later, the copy says rest is holy, and no leader is assigned. A gentle 90-day check-in card is created instead.
After tapping: a confirmation with the leader's name, the day they will hear from them, and a one-paragraph picture of a first Sunday. An email copy goes to the person.

blocks.text: The prototype used one energy scale for everything, which made Faithful hollow (it was just ranks three and four) and forced two Wearying areas onto people who had none. Version 2 adds a readiness dimension and absolute thresholds.

items: 36 energy items: three per archetype, the strongest three from the tested bank of 48 (full list in Appendix A). Five-point scale, "I would struggle here" to "I would thrive here."

2 consistency items: two earlier statements repeated in different words near the end. A gap of three or more points on either flags the result internally as quick answers. The person never sees the flag; the leader sees a small note on the card.

Readiness check: for the five highest-energy archetypes, one question with four answers: Yes, and I'm good at it (ready); Some, and I'd like to grow (learning); No, but I'd try it (willing); No, and I'd rather not (no).

rows: Energy 3.8 or higher AND readiness is ready, learning, or willing. Labeled Ready Now or With A Little Training.
Energy 2.8 to 3.7 AND readiness is ready or learning. Capable, not energized. This is the real pinch-hit list.
Energy 2.4 or lower. No readiness check needed.
Everything else. Named honestly as middle ground, not forced into a bucket.

items: Fallback: if fewer than one Fruitful area clears the threshold, promote the highest-energy area whose readiness is not no, and label it Emerging.
Honesty rule: if nothing scores 2.4 or lower, the result says "No strong drains showed up," rather than inventing weariness.
Straight-lining: if 30 or more of 38 items share the same answer, the result is still shown, but the card notes "answered uniformly; worth a conversation."

blocks.text: Roles live in a catalog file (Appendix B is the template). Each role carries: team, one-line description, tags for the archetypes it fits, audience tags, Sunday or weekday, time cost, minimum commitment, training provided, and the leader who owns follow-up.

items: Candidates: every role tagged with either of the person's two Fruitful archetypes.

Score each candidate: +3 if it matches the primary archetype, +2 for the secondary, +2 for each audience tag the person chose, +1 if it is a Sunday role and the person chose Sunday mornings only, +1 if it is low commitment and the person chose life is very full, +1 if it belongs to a pilot team (pilot phase only).
Show the top three. Never pad with roles that scored zero.
Rest and healing: show the roles, swap the button to Save For Later, create the 90-day check-in card, assign no leader.
Already serving and re-evaluating: same matching, plus a line inviting them to talk with their current leader first; the card goes to General so Sam can broker the conversation.

blocks.text: A single serverless function on Netlify receives the completed result and does five things in Planning Center People. Secrets never touch the browser.

rows: Find the person by email; create them if new (first name, last name, email)
Dedupe by email, so a retake updates rather than duplicates
Write custom fields on a Thrive tab
Thrive Date, Fruitful, Faithful, Wearying, Top Archetype 1 and 2, Availability, Drawn To, Role Chosen, Quick Answers flag
Create a workflow card in the matching workflow
Thrive: Worship (Anil), Thrive: Family Ministries (Morgan), or Thrive: General (Nincy or Kaley)
Add a note to the card
Plain-English summary: the two Fruitful areas, the role chosen with its time cost, availability, drawn-to, and a suggested first Sunday
From LOFT, with the leader's name and the picture of a first Sunday

blocks.text: Planning Center setup (Nincy and Sam, before build week ends)

items: Create a People custom tab named Thrive with the fields above (text fields are fine; Availability and Fruitful can be single-select if you prefer clean reporting).

Create three People workflows: Thrive: Worship, Thrive: Family Ministries, Thrive: General. Each has four steps: 1) Contact within 48 hours, 2) First Serve scheduled, 3) First Serve completed, 4) 30-day check-in. Assign step 1 to the leader.
Confirm Anil and Morgan have People access sufficient to see and complete workflow cards, and that workflow email notifications are on for them.
Create the Personal Access Token (done) and enter Client ID and Secret into Netlify as environment variables PCO_CLIENT_ID and PCO_SECRET. Sam does this step himself; nobody else needs the secret.
Privacy: Planning Center is the only data store. The function logs a timestamp and success or failure only, never names or emails.

blocks.text: The tool creates the card. The leader creates the relationship. This is the part that determines whether anything gets used.

rows: Text first, not email. "Hi Priya, it's Anil from the Worship Team. Thrive said you're wired for this, and I'd love to have you shadow us one Sunday. Does the 21st or the 28th work?"
Send the First Serve details: where to park, what time, who will meet them, what they will and won't be asked to do. No commitment beyond that one Sunday.
Meet them at the door personally. Give them one real, small thing to do. Introduce them to two people by name. Thank them before they leave.
One text: "How did it feel? Want to keep going, try something else, or pause?" All three answers are good answers.
Step 4 complete, with the answer in the note

blocks.text: Sam's part: a ten-minute briefing with Anil and Morgan before the pilot lunch, and a five-minute check at SLT each week on cards that are stuck at step 1.

items: Repository: github.com/loftcitychurch/thrive (or under Sam's account to start). Version control, history, and browser editing for content files.
Site: static HTML, CSS, and JavaScript modules. No framework, no build step. Fast on phones, easy for Claude Code to maintain.

Content as data: /content/en/items.json, archetypes.json, roles.json, teams.json, ui.json. Changing a team name, a time cost, or a book means editing a JSON file, not code. /content/es/ is scaffolded from day one for Spanish.
Backend: one Netlify Function, /netlify/functions/submit.js, holding the Planning Center calls and the confirmation email.
Hosting: Netlify, deployed automatically from the main branch. DNS: CNAME thrive pointing to the Netlify site, same pattern as study.loftcity.church.
Accessibility: 18px base text, 44px tap targets, labeled controls, works without JavaScript for the first screen.
Retire the prototype: once Quick Fit is live, the old page redirects to thrive.loftcity.church.

rows: Planning Center tab and workflows; role catalog filled in for Worship and Family Ministries (Appendix B); repo created; content JSON drafted from this spec; DNS record added

sections.h: Open items that need a person, not a developer

items: Real time costs for every Worship and Family Ministries role (Appendix B). This is the single most important content in the tool and only Anil and Morgan know it.
Who owns Thrive: General during the pilot (Nincy or Kaley).
The date of the next welcome lunch, which sets the build deadline.
GitHub account: create one for LOFT (recommended) or use Sam's.
Confirm Anil and Morgan are comfortable with text-first follow-up and know the two Sundays they will offer.
